papers.title: Innovation collaborative et participative dans les services publics. Dynamiques et perspectives dans le secteur de la santé
papers.abstract: Cet article analyse les dynamiques des innovations collaboratives et participatives dans les services publics de santé, en s’appuyant sur la typologie de Chen et al. (2020). À partir d’une enquête mixte portant sur des projets labellisés dans le cadre du dispositif national « Droits des usagers de la santé », l’étude montre que les innovations impliquant la participation des usagers sont principalement opérationnelles et capacitaires, mobilisant fréquemment des partenariats externes. L’analyse révèle l’importance cruciale des interactions entre dynamiques internes et externes de ces innovations et identifie les conditions essentielles à leur réussite : mobilisation efficace des ressources internes, soutien institutionnel solide, et participation précoce et active des usagers. L’analyse souligne néanmoins des limites, notamment dans l’implication des citoyens, et ouvre des perspectives pour mieux comprendre comment renforcer la cocréation dans les services publics afin de maximiser la valeur publique.

papers.title: Framework for Sustainable Water Management in Some Selected States in Northern Nigeria
papers.abstract: Both groundwater and surface water are the most reliable sources for domestic, agricultural, and industrial use in Nigeria. However, they face increasing pressure from above-ground human activities, such as uncontrolled urbanization, continuous waste disposal, and poor land-use management. The impact on water users is unacceptable, and the purely technical solutions of this century have failed to address the growing contamination of this vital resource. This study examines existing issues in groundwater management and provides a platform for engaging various stakeholders whose involvement is necessary to address these problems. The steps taken to identify and involve stakeholders responsible for and affected by both surface and groundwater contamination are described and discussed. The paper assesses current water management approaches, the causes of contamination, stakeholders’ capacities and concerns, and offers sustainable solutions that will help transition from the current system to a more integrated and effective one. Sustainable strategies suitable for many developing countries are also recommended. The findings will contribute valuable insights to water managers, policymakers, and decision-makers working to implement sustainable groundwater management systems in Nigeria and other rapidly developing nations.

papers.title: Auditee and Auditor Factors Affecting Audit Delay with Audit Firm Reputation as Moderating Variable: Supporting SDG 16 in Tourism Firms
papers.abstract: Objective: To examine the effects of auditee and auditor factors on audit delay and evaluates whether audit firm reputation moderates these relationships. The analysis focuses on tourism, restaurant, and hotel companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, while linking timely audited reporting to the transparency and accountability principles of Sustainable Development Goal 16. Method: The study employed a quantitative explanatory design using secondary data from audited annual reports for 2017–2021. Purposive sampling yielded 22 companies and 110 firm-year observations. Liquidity, firm size, financial distress, and audit opinion were tested as explanatory variables, while audit firm reputation was examined through moderated regression analysis. Results: Liquidity had no significant effect on audit delay. Firm size and financial distress significantly increased audit delay, whereas an unqualified audit opinion reduced the reporting lag. Audit firm reputation did not moderate the liquidity–audit delay relationship but significantly moderated the effects of firm size, financial distress, and audit opinion. Novelty: The study integrates auditee financial characteristics and auditor-related attributes within a single moderation model in a sector observed across pre-pandemic and pandemic periods. It extends audit-delay research by demonstrating that reputable audit firms do not uniformly accelerate reporting; their moderating role depends on the underlying company characteristic. The findings offer sector-specific evidence relevant to stronger corporate reporting discipline and the accountability orientation of SDG 16.
papers.venue: Journal of Current Studies in SDGs

papers.title: Epidemiologia de 376.383 confecções de fístulas arteriovenosas para hemodiálise ao longo de 9 anos no Sistema Único de Saúde e no setor privado brasileiro
authors: Júlia Freire Castanheira de Paiva Ferreira
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine trends in AVF creation for hemodialysis across Brazil from 2015 to 2023, assessing differences in frequency, geographic distribution, and sectoral disparities between the public and private healthcare sectors. METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using anonymized data from national administrative databases: DATASUS (public sector) and D-TISS (private sector). The majority of AVF creation procedures were included. Statistical analyses considered regional adjustments and were performed using SPSS v.20, with significance set at p < 0.001. RESULTS: Over the nine- year period, 376,383 AVF procedures were recorded, with 90.57% occurring in the public sector. While the absolute number of AVF creations increased, the ratio of AVFs per 1,000 dialysis patients showed a declining trend. Regional disparities were evident, with the Southeast and South regions presenting higher procedure rates compared to other areas. The private sector consistently reported lower creation rates. CONCLUSION: Although, separately, dialysis and AVF rates have risen steadily in Brazil, the relative rate between them has shown a decreasing trend over the years. The predominance of AVF procedures in the public system is more pronounced.

papers.title: GC×GC–MS analysis of volatile components extracted by spinning cone column from Forsythia suspensa and its antimicrobial assessment
papers.abstract: Forsythia suspensa is a traditional medicinal plant rich in volatile bioactive compounds with important pharmacological and application value. In this study, volatile compounds from F. suspensa were extracted using spinning cone column (SCC) technology for the first time. The compounds were qualitatively characterized using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) and comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC×GC–MS), as well as quantified using the area normalization method. The antibacterial activity of the resulting essential oil against six pathogenic microorganisms was evaluated using the broth microdilution method. The essential oil yield obtained through SCC extraction reached 2.16%. A total of 38 compounds were identified from the essential oil, with β-pinene, 4-terpinenol, sabinene, and α-pinene as the major constituents. The GC×GC–MS analysis enabled the detection of 90 compounds, including those identified by GC–MS, and revealed additional bioactive compounds, such as guaiacol, myrtenal, citronellol, carvacrol, and α-bisabolol, that were not detected by GC–MS. The antimicrobial assays demonstrated that the essential oil exhibited antimicrobial activity against susceptible test microorganisms, with minimum inhibitory concentration values ranging from 31.3 μg/mL to 62.5 μg/mL. These findings highlighted the potential of SCC technology for extracting F. suspensa essential oil and demonstrated the value of GC×GC–MS for comprehensive characterization of its volatile constituents, providing a basis for further investigation of its antibacterial potential.

papers.title: Effect Of Thiamine Pyrophosphate as an Adjunct to Metformin in Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized, Controlled Pilot Clinical Trial
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia and an increased risk of cardiovascular and microvascular complications. Functional thiamine deficiency and altered activity of thiamine-dependent enzymes have been implicated in the metabolic dysregulation associated with diabetes. Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), the biologically active form of vitamin B1, plays a central role in mitochondrial glucose metabolism and may contribute to improved metabolic control. A randomized, placebo-controlled pilot clinical trial was conducted to evaluate the effect of TPP as an adjunct treatment to metformin in patients with T2DM with inadequate glycaemic control. Twenty-seven participants receiving stable metformin therapy were randomly assigned to receive weekly intravenous TPP or placebo for 12 weeks. Anthropometric, hemodynamic, and biochemical variables were assessed, including glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting glucose, and lipid profile. Inflammatory markers were also analysed. Both within-group and between-group statistical analyses were performed. Results: Twenty-seven patients were included in the final analysis. The intervention group showed a significant reduction in HbA1c (-7.4%, p = 0.003) and systolic blood pressure (-5.3%, p = 0.032). Other metabolic and inflammatory parameters showed favourable trends without reaching statistical significance. The intervention was well tolerated, and no serious adverse events were reported. Adjunctive therapy with thiamine pyrophosphate demonstrated promising effects on glycaemic control and hemodynamic parameters in patients with T2DM treated with metformin. These findings support the need for larger randomized clinical trials to confirm the potential therapeutic role of TPP in diabetes management.
papers.venue: Biomedical Journal of Scientific & Technical Research

papers.title: Risk committees and corporate disclosure: Evidence on risk and sustainability reporting with governance moderation
papers.abstract: Environmental and social concerns related to sustainability can represent non-financial risks requiring effective risk management (Wong, 2014). In this context, risk committees may play a role in overseeing such risks and their related corporate disclosures. This study investigates how risk committees impact both risk and sustainability disclosure, aiming to understand how corporate governance enhances transparency and investor confidence. It also examines whether board size, independence, and institutional ownership moderate these relationships, influencing the effectiveness of risk committees in corporate reporting. Using a quantitative approach, this study analyzed 807 samples from Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) companies that published sustainability reports between 2019 and 2023. The results show that risk committees positively influence risk disclosure but do not significantly affect sustainability disclosure. Moderation analysis indicates that board size and independence weaken the effect on risk disclosure. Conversely, institutional ownership strengthens the impact on sustainability disclosure, but not on risk disclosure. These findings suggest risk committees are more effective for traditional risk reporting than for sustainability transparency. This study provides new insights by testing the effectiveness of risk committees in enhancing both types of disclosures. It offers practical insights for regulators, investors, and corporate leaders, underscoring the importance of risk committees in improving disclosure quality to foster transparency and trust.

papers.title: Orsellinic acid derivatives with antibacterial activity from Alternaria sp. TY22 associated with Typha orientalis
papers.abstract: Filamentous fungi are renowned for producing structurally diverse secondary metabolites with significant biological activities. In the present study, seven compounds, including a pair of new isomeric 2,3-butylene orsellinate derivatives (1a/1b) and five known compounds (2–6), were isolated from the endophytic fungus Alternaria sp. TY22 derived from Typha orientalis. Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analysis. Antibacterial evaluation revealed that 2 and 3 showed strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis with MIC values ranging from 4 to 16 μg/mL, and the new isomers 1a/1b displayed moderate antibacterial activity with MIC values of 64 and 32 μg/mL against S. aureus and B. subtilis, respectively.

papers.title: Gastroprotective potential of Bixa orellana: A critical review of extract-specific phytochemistry and preclinical evidence
papers.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease remains clinically important despite effective Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication and acid-suppressive therapy. Gastric injury reflects an imbalance between aggressive factors, including acid-pepsin activity, H. pylori, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), ethanol, oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and microvascular disturbance and protective mechanisms such as mucus-bicarbonate secretion, prostaglandin signaling, nitric oxide-regulated blood flow, epithelial restitution, and endogenous antioxidant defenses. Bixa orellana L. (annatto or achiote) is a tropical medicinal plant whose seed arils are rich in the apocarotenoids bixin and norbixin, whereas its leaves contain variable phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, terpenoids, alkaloids, and other constituents depending on geography, maturity, and extraction method. This critical narrative review uses a structured search and qualitative evidence-appraisal framework to evaluate extract-specific phytochemistry, direct gastric evidence, indirectly relevant gastrointestinal and vascular evidence, mechanistic plausibility, safety, quality control, and translational readiness. The available literature supports B. orellana as a biologically plausible preclinical mucosal-protective candidate, particularly for prevention of acute chemical injury; however, it does not establish clinical efficacy or chronic ulcer-healing activity. Confidence is limited by the small number of direct gastric studies, incomplete chemical characterization, inconsistent separation of leaf and seed evidence, limited dose-response testing, narrow model selection, and insufficient mechanistic and histological endpoints. Future studies should use authenticated plant material, voucher specimens, chromatographic fingerprints, quantitative markers, complementary prevention and healing models, acute and repeated-dose toxicology, mucus and prostaglandin measurements, oxidative and inflammatory biomarkers, and blinded histological scoring before human investigation is justified.

papers.title: Analysis of the physical properties of incorporating cannabis oil in products for the control of alveolitis
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the incorporation of Cannabis sativa oil into dental formulations designed for the management of alveolitis, a common postoperative complication characterized by severe pain and inflammation following tooth extraction. The aim was to determine whether cannabis oil, modifies essential physical properties compared with eugenol, traditionally used in alveolitis dressings. Two experimental groups were prepared, both combined with tetracycline: one with full-spectrum cannabis oil and the other with eugenol. The materials were subjected to standardized flow, radiopacity, and solubility tests according to ISO guidelines. Flow was measured using standardized discs; radiopacity was assessed by occlusal radiographs with an aluminum step wedge; and solubility was tested using Teflon molds under controlled temperature and humidity conditions. The results demonstrated that the association of tetracycline and cannabis oil exhibited significantly greater flow than the tetracycline-eugenol group, indicating improved adaptability of the material to the alveolar socket. Radiopacity analysis revealed no statistical difference between groups, remaining within clinically acceptable ranges. The solubility test could not be completed, since both materials failed to set under the experimental conditions. It is concluded that replacing eugenol with cannabis oil in dental formulations did not compromise radiopacity and provided superior flow, a desirable characteristic for clinical adaptation. These findings suggest that Cannabis sativa oil formulations may represent a promising alternative for alveolitis management. However, further studies on biocompatibility, antimicrobial activity, and clinical efficacy are required to confirm its applicability in routine dental practice. Keywords: Cannabis sativa, cannabinoids, CBD, pain management, inflammation.

papers.title: Cosmetic Recontouring And Digital Planning: A Smart Strategy For Aesthetic Transformations
papers.abstract: Introduction: Cosmetic recontouring is a relevant technique in aesthetic dentistry, standing out for its conservative approach by correcting imperfections in anterior teeth without the need for significant tooth reduction. Digital planning has further enhanced these treatments, enabling greater personalization and precision in the restorative process. Objective: To present the treatment of an incisal edge fracture in anterior teeth using a minimally invasive approach. Case Report: This report describes the treatment of a dental polytrauma involving multiple incisal edge fractures, in which the planning was carried out virtually using the Digital Smile Design (DSD) protocol. Cosmetic recontouring was performed to restore the anterior teeth, using the silicone index technique as a guide. Conclusion: The application of a minimally invasive approach allowed for precise and efficient execution of the restoration, yielding satisfactory aesthetic results while preserving the original tooth structure to the greatest extent possible. Keywords: Esthetics, Dental. Health Sciences, Technology, and Innovation Management. Dental Impression Materials. Composite Resins. Dental Restoration, Permanent.

papers.title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
papers.abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food innovation, biotechnology, functional foods, nutrigenomics, sustainability, food safety, culinary heritage

papers.title: Modification of the Proximity Indexed Value Method Based on Distance-Based Normalization to Improve the Stability of Alternative Rankings
papers.abstract: The Proximity Indexed Value (PIV) method provides a proximity-based mechanism for ranking alternatives in multi-criteria decision-making; however, its ranking results can be affected by the normalization process and the relative characteristics of criterion values. This study proposes a Distance-Based Proximity Indexed Value (D-PIV) method by incorporating distance-based normalization into the PIV framework to represent the proximity of alternatives to criterion-specific ideal conditions more explicitly. The proposed method was evaluated using an alternative location selection dataset comprising eight alternatives and six criteria, including one cost criterion and five benefit criteria. The evaluation included comparative ranking analysis using 36 systematic criterion-weight perturbation scenarios with changes of ±0.05, ±0.10, and ±0.15. The results show that D-PIV changes the ordering of Loc 3 and Loc 8 compared with conventional PIV, resulting in a ranking that fully corresponds to the reference ranking. The Spearman correlation increased from 0.9762 for PIV to 1.0000 for D-PIV. However, the sensitivity analysis indicates that the distance-based modification does not uniformly improve ranking stability across all alternatives. D-PIV increases the stability of Loc 8 from 69.44% to 72.22%, while lower stability is observed for Loc 3 and Loc 6 compared with PIV. These findings demonstrate that D-PIV contributes a reference-oriented normalization mechanism that improves baseline ranking consistency while redistributing, rather than uniformly eliminating, sensitivity to criterion-weight variations. The study therefore provides both a methodological contribution through the integration of distance-based normalization into PIV and an empirical contribution through systematic evidence of its effects on ranking agreement and stability.
papers.venue: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making

papers.title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.

papers.title: The Impact of Digital Literacy-Based Assignments on Students’ Mastery of Islamic Education and Learning Habits: A Multivariate Regression Analysis
papers.abstract: ENGLISH: The Impact of Digital Literacy-Based Assignments on Students’ Mastery of Islamic Education and Learning Habits: A Multivariate Regression AnalysisObjective: This study aims to analyze the simultaneous effects of digital literacy assignments on the mastery of Islamic Education material on the theme of tolerance and learning habits of eighth-grade students at SMPN 08 Lebong. Method: This study uses a quantitative approach with survey methods and multivariate regression analysis to test the relationship between digital literacy, mastery of material, and learning habits. Results: Digital literacy-based assignments significantly influence both variables, contributing 42.8% to mastery of the material and 13.2% to learning habits. Conclusion: Digital literacy effectively improves mastery of Islamic Education material, but its influence on learning habits still requires support from other holistic strategies. Contribution: This study suggests that digital assignments should emphasize the learning habit formation process and the reinforcement of Islamic character values. These findings contribute to developing technology-based curricula relevant to Islamic education in the digital age.INDONESIAN: Pengaruh Penugasan Melalui Literasi Digital terhadap Penguasaan Materi PAI Tema Toleransi dan Kebiasaan Belajar Siswa: Analisis Regresi MultivariatTujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh penugasan melalui literasi digital terhadap penguasaan materi Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) tema toleransi dan kebiasaan belajar siswa kelas VIII SMPN 08 Lebong secara simultan. Metode: Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei dan analisis regresi multivariat untuk menguji hubungan antara variabel literasi digital, penguasaan materi, dan kebiasaan belajar. Hasil: Penugasan berbasis literasi digital memberikan pengaruh signifikan terhadap kedua variabel, dengan kontribusi sebesar 42,8% terhadap penguasaan materi dan 13,2% terhadap kebiasaan belajar. Kesimpulan: Literasi digital efektif dalam meningkatkan penguasaan materi PAI, namun pengaruhnya terhadap kebiasaan belajar masih memerlukan dukungan strategi lain yang lebih holistik. Kontribusi: Penelitian ini menyarankan agar penugasan digital didesain dengan penekanan pada proses pembiasaan belajar dan penguatan nilai-nilai karakter Islami. Temuan ini memberikan kontribusi penting bagi pengembangan kurikulum berbasis teknologi yang relevan dengan pendidikan Islam di era digital.

papers.title: “Calcare Cavernoso” as a key predisposing factor for sinkhole occurrence in Tuscany (Italy): inventory update, remote sensing detection, and GIS–ML susceptibility modelling
papers.abstract: The “Calcare Cavernoso” (cavernous limestone) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence. This study investigates the spatial relationship between sinkholes and the distribution of “Calcare Cavernoso” in Tuscany (Italy) and updates the regional subset of the ISPRA national sinkhole database. An integrated approach combined bibliographic information, targeted field surveys, historical cartography, and multi-source geospatial datasets. Geological and thematic layers were retrieved from the Tuscany “Geoscopio” portal, while Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery was processed using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) to support the detection of flooded sinkholes. Historical maps were exploited to infer sinkhole persistence and potential evolutionary trends, including partial or complete infilling. All thematic layers (geology, faults, hydrography, quarries, mines, topography, and sinkholes) were harmonized, georeferenced, and rasterized on a 250 × 250 m grid within an ESRI ArcGIS environment. Susceptibility modelling was implemented using density-based proxies and an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) framework, producing probability outputs subsequently grouped into classes to enhance operational usability. The results substantially expand the regional sinkhole inventory (from 88 to 1223 mapped features) and support a strong spatial association between sinkhole occurrence and “Calcare Cavernoso”, further corroborated by targeted field checks. The most influential susceptibility drivers include “Calcare Cavernoso”, low-slope settings, DTM-derived parameters, fault density, and anthropogenic underground activities (quarries and mines), while other variables show secondary or more complex contributions.

papers.title: Anthropogenic sinkholes in the urban fabric of Messina (Sicily, Italy)
papers.abstract: Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina (Sicily, Italy), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain. We present an updated, georeferenced inventory of sinkholes within the municipal urban area, built from local press/ web sources and field cross-checks, and we assess spatial relationships with culverted drainage and known urban cavity entrances. To frame site-effects in a seismic setting, we consult the Italian catalogue of earthquake-induced ground failures (CEDIT) and the Italian catalogue of earthquake environmental effects (EEE), which document widespread ground cracking, settlement and liquefaction during major historical earthquakes, notably the 1908 Messina event. Our results highlight clusters along culverted stream corridors and in zones influenced by underground legacy, supporting future scenario-based prioritization of inspections and post-event checks.

papers.title: Mapping natural sinkhole susceptibility in Italy: integrating a national inventory with machine learning
papers.abstract: Natural sinkholes are a widespread geohazard in Italy, complicating landuse planning and risk reduction. This study develops the first national-scale susceptibility map for natural sinkholes using an updated inventory and data-driven modelling. Building on the ISPRA National Sinkhole Database, we assembled more than 14,000 documented features from literature, historical records, imagery and regional datasets. Geological, geomorphological, structural, hydrogeological and geochemical factors were converted into gridded predictors and combined with the inventory through a machine-learning regression framework estimating a continuous susceptibility score. The calibrated model, evaluated on a held-out 20% test subset, produces a susceptibility surface for the Italian territory. Interpretation tools emphasize the importance of soluble rocks, fault-controlled permeability, deep gas emissions and mineralized springs, consistent with previous studies. High-susceptibility zones align with major karst and evaporitic provinces, including the Friuli-Veneto piedmont, northern Apulia, Latium travertine basins and central Sicilian evaporites, whereas western Alpine sectors and Sardinia show very low scores. The map offers a coherent national overview of where natural sinkholes are more likely to occur and provides an operational basis for prioritizing surveys, monitoring programmes and planning measures, while the methodology can be refined to incorporate time-dependent drivers and multi-hazard interactions. These advances support more resilient and sustainable territorial development.
papers.venue: Rendiconti online della Società Geologica Italiana

papers.title: Using Photography as a Tool for Critical Urban Diagnosis: An Undomestication Strategy
papers.abstract: This research describes a teaching experience of urbanism using photography as a critical pedagogical strategy of educating the look to raise awareness among undergraduate students about the problems of their context, employing the objective worldview of each participant regarding their perception of the city and understanding their role as knowledge builders.This was a descriptive field research, based on participant observation methodology, structured in four stages, through a process of categorizing photographs taken by the attendees, shaping positive and negative aspects of the experience.Information obtained was correlated on a database for visualizing the study data through opensource software, with the final identification of the main phenomena.Through this process, a significant disparity was detected in the perception of the observers; therefore, the importance of promoting other educational practices that can raise awareness among architecture and urbanism students about the different urban singularities present in the built environment of developing countries.
